svg.title: Anatomy of a Dataverse Web API request and response
svg.desc: The request line GET https://cedar-dev.crm4.dynamics.com/api/data/v9.2/cedar_workorders followed by query options is split into labelled parts: environment URL, the Web API path /api/data/, the version v9.2, the entity set name cedar_workorders, and the query options $select, $filter, $orderby and $expand. Below it the request headers: Authorization Bearer token from lesson 73, Accept application/json, OData-MaxVersion 4.0, OData-Version 4.0, If-None-Match null, and optional Prefer values for page size and formatted values. The response shows status 200 OK, the header Preference-Applied, and a JSON body with @odata.context, a value array of rows, each with @odata.etag, the selected columns, a formatted value annotation next to the numeric choice value, the lookup value property _cedar_site_value and the expanded cedar_Site object, and at the end @odata.nextLink when more rows exist. A side box maps HTTP methods to operations: POST creates or calls an action, GET retrieves or calls a function, PATCH updates or upserts, DELETE deletes, PUT sets a single column.
svg.text: One request, read part by part
environment URL • /api/data/ = Web API path • v9.2 = version • cedar_workorders = entity set name (plural) • ?… = query options
POST create a row; call an action
GET retrieve rows; call a function
PATCH update a row (upsert unless If-Match: *)
DELETE delete a row, a column value or a link
Bodies are JSON with Content-Type: application/json.
etag = row version • annotation = label for people • _…_value = lookup ID • nextLink = more pages: follow it unchanged
